entry.title: MicroAssert: Microarchitecture-Aware Structured Assertion Generation for CPU Verification
entry.summary:
Automatic assertion generation reduces manual verification effort, yet existing approaches struggle to capture microarchitectural behaviors and cross-region interactions in CPUs. We present MicroAssert, a microarchitecture-aware framework that identifies functional regions directly from RTL and generates local and composite assertions through structured contracts and deterministic verification primitives. Coverage-guided feedback further improves verification completeness by progressively expanding proof-relevant RTL coverage.

Source: arXiv CS (PL, SE, DB, DC, DS) · Tags: #compilers #distributed-systems #computer-architecture #software-architecture

entry.title: Rethinking Zero-Knowledge TLS: Proof of Protocol Execution and the Reclaim Protocol
entry.summary:
In a zkTLS protocol, a user proves to a third party a property of data obtained from an online service over TLS, revealing nothing beyond the statement proven. Each existing scheme, however, comes with its own security model, written for that scheme alone, so the schemes are not proven secure against a common definition. The root cause is a mismatch of levels: existing models are stated at the level of TLS and therefore reflect how each construction handles it.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #rust #distributed-systems

entry.title: Aker: Efficient Two-Party SLH-DSA
entry.summary:
Threshold signing is widely deployed to protect cryptographic keys, but extending these deployments to post-quantum signatures remains challenging. While NIST's lattice-based signatures now have efficient threshold protocols, distributed signing for SLH-DSA (FIPS 205), NIST's stateless hash-based signature standard, has been considered prohibitively expensive because it lacks the algebraic structure those protocols typically exploit. We present Aker, a maliciously secure two-party signing protocol compatible with an unmodified FIPS 205 verifier.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #distributed-systems #post-quantum

entry.title: Polycentrality in Urban Socioecological Systems: A Multilayer Analysis of Social Infrastructure in Iztapalapa, Mexico City
entry.summary:
The spatial distribution of infrastructure and activities, along with the networks and interactions that connect them, is key to understanding the relationship between urban form, function, and sustainability from a complex systems perspective. Within this dynamic relationship, the extent to which localized social infrastructure can reinforce existing functional centralities or create conditions for the emergence of new ones remains insufficiently understood. This study examines these relationships through the UTOPÍAS program in Iztapalapa, Mexico City, where 15 public social facilities have been established across a historically underserved urban territory.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #distributed-systems
